summary:
[  edit  ]
The WebSocket  DAT  receives and parses  WebSocket  messages. WebSockets are fast an efficient two way communication protocol used by web servers and clients. Each message is parsed and appended as a row in the  DAT 's table. The table is FIFO "first-in first-out" and limited to parameter-set number of lines. An optional script may be run for each packet received. Secure (tls) websocket servers are also supported.
Connections to different WebSocket sites are supported without requiring manual header setup.
The WebSocket  DAT  prints status and error messages to the TouchDesigner text console. The text console can be enabled by setting the environment variable TOUCH_TEXT_CONSOLE=1 (see:  https://docs.derivative.ca/Variables#System_Environment_Variables ). The text console will open the next time TouchDesigner is launched.
For SocketIO support see the  SocketIO DAT .
See also:  TCP/IP DAT
Example project:  chat with WebSockets

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: While on, the  DAT  receives information sent to the network port. While Off, no updating occurs. Data sent to the port is lost.

parameters.label: Network Address
parameters.name: netaddress
parameters.description: The network address of the server computer. This address is a standard WWW address, such as  foo  or  foo.bar.com . You can put an IP address (e.g.  100.123.45.78 ). If you put  localhost , it means the other end of the connection is on the same computer.

parameters.label: Network Port
parameters.name: port
parameters.description: The port in which the  DAT  will accept messages.	Port 443 implies a secure connection. If attempting a secure connection not using port 443 then a "wss://" prefix is required on the Network Address parameter.

parameters.label: Connection Timeout
parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds the WebSocket  DAT  will wait to connect to the server. Note: this is an upper limit and the connection may fail before the connection timeout is reached.

parameters.label: Callbacks  DAT
parameters.name: callbacks
parameters.description: The Callbacks  DAT  will execute once for each message coming in.

parameters.label: Execute from
parameters.name: executeloc
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines the location the script is run from.

parameters.label: Current  Node
parameters.name: current
parameters.description: The script is executed from the current node location.

parameters.label: Callbacks  DAT
parameters.name: callbacks
parameters.description: The script is executed from the location of the  DAT  specified in the Callbacks  DAT  parameter.

parameters.label: Specified  Operator
parameters.name: op
parameters.description: The script is executed from the operator specified in the From Operator parameter below.

parameters.label: From  Operator
parameters.name: fromop
parameters.description: The operator whose state change will trigger the  DAT  to execute its script when Execute from is set to Specified  Operator . This operator is also the path that the script will be executed from if the Execute from parameter is set to Specified  Operator .

parameters.label: Clamp Output
parameters.name: clamp
parameters.description: The  DAT  is limited to 100 messages by default but with Clamp Output, this can be set to anything including unlimited.

parameters.label: Maximum Lines
parameters.name: maxlines
parameters.description: Limits the number of messages, older messages are removed from the list first.

parameters.label: Clear Output
parameters.name: clear
parameters.description: Deletes all lines except the heading. To clear with a python script  op( "opname" ).par.clear.pulse()

parameters.label: Bytes Column
parameters.name: bytes
parameters.description: Outputs the raw bytes of the message in a separate column.
